source_constraint: All expected outputs and expectations are grounded exclusively in docs.sui.io, move-book.com, and the MystenLabs/sui-stack-hello-world repository. Graders should flag any claims sourced from third-party blogs, tutorials, or unofficial documentation.

evals.prompt: How can I install Sui?
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step installation instructions starting with suiup as the recommended method, plus alternatives for different platforms.
expectations: The response recommends suiup as the primary installation method
The response includes the suiup install command: curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MystenLabs/suiup/main/install.sh | sh
The response shows how to install a network-specific version: suiup install sui@testnet or suiup install sui@mainnet
The response mentions suiup switch sui@testnet to make the installed version the active default
The response mentions Homebrew (brew install sui) and Chocolatey (choco install sui) as alternatives
The response mentions that alternatives do not support installing additional Sui Stack components
The response includes sui --version for verifying installation
The response notes the Windows caveat: the curl | sh command requires a Unix shell; Windows users should use Chocolatey or WSL

evals.prompt: My sui --version shows 1.67.3 but the latest is 1.69. I installed via suiup. How do I update?
evals.expected_output: Instructions for updating AND switching Sui via suiup, explaining the two-step process.
expectations: The response provides the update command: suiup update sui@testnet (or sui@mainnet depending on their target)
The response explicitly warns that suiup update downloads the new version but does NOT automatically make it the active default
The response provides the switch command: suiup switch sui@testnet to make the updated version active
The response explains that the CLI version should match the target network
The response suggests running suiup show to verify which version is active
The response does not use nonexistent commands like 'suiup use' or 'suiup default'
The response does not suggest reinstalling from scratch when suiup update + switch is sufficient

evals.prompt: I get this error when building: '[NOTE] Updating dependencies for testnet environment because Move.toml has been changed. Packages with old dependencies found.' What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that the CLI version is behind the network, with the correct update and switch commands.
expectations: The response identifies this as a CLI version mismatch with the target network
The response suggests running suiup update sui@testnet followed by suiup switch sui@testnet
The response mentions the new package management format introduced in Sui CLI v1.63
The response does NOT suggest adding or modifying a Sui = { git = ... } dependency line — the Sui framework is resolved automatically on current CLI versions
The response mentions migrating from the old [addresses] format to the new [environments] section if applicable

evals.prompt: I get 'Cannot upgrade package without having a published id'. I already published it before. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of the v1.63 package management migration and how Published.toml tracks published addresses.
expectations: The response explains that this error relates to the new package management system introduced in Sui CLI v1.63
The response explains that published addresses are now tracked in Published.toml, not inside Move.toml
The response explains that if the user migrated from the old format, they need to ensure Published.toml exists with the correct published-at and upgrade-capability-id
The response does not tell the user to manually edit Move.toml with a published-at field (that's the old format)
The response mentions that the UpgradeCap object ID is needed for the upgrade command

evals.prompt: I get 'error[E13001]: feature is not supported in specified edition' when I use 'public struct'. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that the public struct syntax requires edition = 2024 in Move.toml.
expectations: The response identifies that the public struct syntax is a Move 2024 feature
The response instructs the user to set edition = "2024" in the [package] section of Move.toml
The response explains that the legacy edition does not support Move 2024 features
The response does not suggest workarounds like removing the public keyword unless the user explicitly wants legacy compatibility

evals.prompt: How do I get SUI tokens for testing? Where is the faucet?
evals.expected_output: Multiple faucet methods including web, CLI, Discord, and SDK, with the official URL.
expectations: The response provides the official faucet URL: faucet.sui.io
The response mentions the CLI method: sui client faucet
The response mentions the Discord method: !faucet <ADDRESS> in #devnet-faucet or #testnet-faucet
The response mentions the TypeScript SDK method: requestSuiFromFaucetV2
The response states that Devnet and Testnet tokens are free and have no monetary value
The response mentions rate limiting and suggests trying alternative faucets if the limit is hit

evals.prompt: How do I create a wallet and fund it with the devnet faucet using only the CLI?
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step CLI commands from first-time setup through funded address.
expectations: The response starts with sui client (or sui client -y) to trigger first-time configuration
The response mentions that this creates a new key pair, address, and recovery phrase
The response warns to save the recovery phrase immediately as it is only displayed once
The response shows how to switch to devnet: sui client switch --env devnet
The response shows how to request tokens: sui client faucet
The response shows how to verify: sui client balance or sui client gas

evals.prompt: How do I publish a Move package for the first time? What do I get back?
evals.expected_output: The publish command, prerequisites, and what the transaction returns.
expectations: The response includes the command: sui client publish
The response mentions prerequisites: successful build (sui move build), active environment set, sufficient SUI balance
The response explains that publishing returns a unique package ID
The response explains that an UpgradeCap object is sent to the publisher's address
The response mentions that object IDs created during init functions appear in the transaction effects
The response mentions that Published.toml is created or updated automatically

evals.prompt: I published to Testnet but now I want to publish a fresh copy to Devnet for development. How do I publish it again to another package ID?
evals.expected_output: Instructions for publishing to a different environment, explaining that each network gives a separate package ID.
expectations: The response explains that each network gives the package a separate, independent package ID
The response instructs the user to switch environments: sui client switch --env devnet
The response explains that Published.toml tracks published addresses per environment
The response mentions getting Devnet tokens from the faucet before publishing
The response does not suggest deleting or modifying Published.toml to force a fresh publish (the toolchain handles multi-environment tracking)

evals.prompt: How do I upgrade a published Move contract on Sui? What's the process?
evals.expected_output: The full upgrade workflow including UpgradeCap, policies, and the CLI command.
expectations: The response explains that published packages are immutable but can be upgraded by publishing a new version
The response mentions the UpgradeCap as the object that controls upgrade authority
The response includes the CLI command: sui client upgrade --upgrade-capability <CAP_ID>
The response describes upgrade policies: compatible (add functions), additive (add modules), dependency-only
The response mentions that the UpgradeCap can be restricted in the same PTB as the publish command
The response mentions the option to destroy the UpgradeCap to make the package permanently immutable

evals.prompt: How do I write and run tests for a Sui Move module? What testing tools are available?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of the test framework, test_scenario, running tests, and coverage.
expectations: The response shows the sui move test command for running tests
The response mentions the #[test] attribute for marking test functions
The response mentions sui::test_scenario for multi-transaction, multi-sender test scenarios
The response mentions std::unit_test for assertion macros
The response mentions sui move test --coverage for tracking code coverage
The response mentions sui move coverage source --module <name> for viewing coverage results

evals.prompt: How do I install and set up Move Analyzer for VS Code?
evals.expected_output: Installation via suiup plus VS Code extension setup.
expectations: The response provides the install command: suiup install move-analyzer
The response instructs the user to install the Move Analyzer extension in VS Code
The response mentions the features: code completion, go-to-definition, diagnostics, hover documentation
The response mentions that it activates automatically for .move files

evals.prompt: I get 'Cannot find gas coin for signer address' when trying to execute a transaction. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of gas coin issues and how to check and fix them.
expectations: The response explains that the error means the address has no SUI coin objects with sufficient balance for gas
The response suggests checking balance with sui client balance or sui client gas
The response suggests getting tokens from the faucet if the balance is zero
The response mentions that if the user has many small coin objects, they may need to merge them
The response does not suggest unrelated fixes like changing code or redeploying

evals.prompt: My dry run is failing on a transaction. What should I check to debug it?
evals.expected_output: A checklist of common dry run failure causes and debugging steps.
expectations: The response mentions checking that all object IDs are correct and exist on the target network
The response mentions checking that the sender has sufficient gas
The response mentions checking that function arguments match the expected types
The response mentions checking that the active environment matches the network where the package is published
The response mentions devInspectTransactionBlock as the SDK method for programmatic dry runs

evals.prompt: How do I start and use a local Sui network for development?
evals.expected_output: The localnet start command, faucet access, and how to switch to it.
expectations: The response includes the command: sui start --with-faucet --force-regenesis (or similar)
The response mentions the local faucet endpoint at 127.0.0.1:5003/gas or 127.0.0.1:9123/gas
The response shows how to switch to localnet: sui client switch --env localnet
The response explains that localnet resets on restart with --force-regenesis
The response mentions that localnet is useful for offline development and rapid iteration

evals.prompt: How do I set up a React frontend for my Sui Move package? What packages do I need?
evals.expected_output: For the hello-world workflow, instructions to use the existing ui app in sui-stack-hello-world, update constants.ts with the package ID, and run it with pnpm.
expectations: The response mentions @mysten/dapp-kit for React components and hooks
The response mentions @mysten/sui as the core TypeScript SDK
The response mentions @tanstack/react-query as a required peer dependency
The response directs hello-world users to the existing sui-stack-hello-world/ui app
The response says not to run npm create @mysten/dapp inside the hello-world project
The response tells the user to update ui/src/constants.ts with the published package ID
The response mentions pnpm as the recommended package manager
The response mentions the ConnectButton component for wallet connection

evals.prompt: How do I serialize a transaction to send to another party for signing, like for a multisig upgrade?
evals.expected_output: Instructions for using --serialize-unsigned-transaction or --serialize-output to generate base64 transaction bytes for offline signing.
expectations: The response mentions the --serialize-unsigned-transaction or --serialize-output flag on sui client commands
The response explains that this outputs base64 transaction bytes instead of executing
The response mentions that these bytes can be sent to other signers for offline signing
The response mentions that this is the standard approach for multisig workflows

evals.prompt: What's the correct Move.toml format? I'm confused about [addresses] vs [environments] and Sui dependencies. I keep getting build errors.
evals.expected_output: An explanation of the current Move.toml format: no explicit Sui dependency, no [addresses], optional [environments].
expectations: The response explains that the Sui framework dependency is resolved automatically and should NOT be specified in [dependencies]
The response warns that using Sui = { git = '...' } in dependencies causes 'legacy system name' errors on current CLI versions
The response explains that [addresses] is no longer needed — the old my_project = '0x0' format is deprecated
The response mentions [environments] as the replacement for multi-network targeting with chain IDs
The response mentions that Published.toml replaces the old published-at field in Move.toml
The response provides a minimal correct Move.toml example with just [package] and edition = '2024'

evals.prompt: I published my package and got objects back. How do I find the package ID and the objects created by init functions?
evals.expected_output: Instructions for finding the package ID and init-created object IDs from the publish transaction output.
expectations: The response explains that the package ID appears in the publish transaction output under created objects
The response mentions that objects created by init functions also appear in the transaction effects
The response suggests using sui client object <OBJECT_ID> to inspect any created object
The response mentions that explorers (SuiVision, Suiscan) can also be used to view the transaction details
The response mentions that Published.toml records the package address for future reference

evals.prompt: Never sign two concurrent transactions that touch the same owned object — I keep hearing this. What happens if I do? How do I avoid it?
evals.expected_output: An explanation of equivocation, object locking until epoch end, and strategies to avoid it.
expectations: The response explains that signing two concurrent transactions on the same owned object causes equivocation
The response explains that equivocation locks the object until the current epoch ends (approximately 24 hours on Mainnet)
The response recommends using independent objects for concurrent operations or waiting for transaction completion before submitting the next
The response mentions that this applies to owned objects specifically, not shared objects
The response does not downplay the severity — this is a real foot-gun that can lock assets for hours

evals.prompt: I ran suiup update sui@testnet and it says it downloaded v1.70.2, but sui --version still shows v1.62.0. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that suiup update downloads but doesn't switch, and the correct command to activate the new version.
expectations: The response explains that suiup update downloads the new version but does not make it the active default
The response provides the fix: suiup switch sui@testnet
The response explains the switch command syntax: binary@network (e.g., sui@testnet, not 'suiup switch sui testnet v1.70.2')
The response suggests suiup show to verify the current default and installed versions
The response does not suggest nonexistent commands like 'suiup use', 'suiup default', or 'suiup set'

evals.prompt: I get a 'client/server api version mismatch' warning when running sui client commands. Client is 1.62.0 and server is 1.70.2. How do I fix this?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that the CLI version is behind the network and needs to be updated and switched.
expectations: The response explains that this warning means the locally installed Sui CLI is older than the network version
The response provides the two-step fix: suiup update sui@testnet followed by suiup switch sui@testnet
The response mentions verifying with sui --version after switching
The response does not suggest ignoring the warning — version mismatches can cause build failures and unexpected behavior

evals.prompt: I installed move-analyzer with suiup but the 'move-analyzer' command isn't found. What do I need to do?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that suiup install downloads but may not set the default, and suiup switch is needed.
expectations: The response explains that after suiup install, the binary may not be set as the active default
The response provides the fix: suiup switch move-analyzer@testnet
The response suggests suiup show to verify installation and default status
The response does not suggest manual PATH manipulation or reinstalling

evals.prompt: I get 'Dependency Sui is a legacy system name and cannot be used' when I run sui move build. My Move.toml has Sui = { git = "https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui.git", subdir = "crates/sui-framework/packages/sui-framework", rev = "framework/testnet" }. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: An explanation that the git-based Sui dependency is no longer valid and should be removed.
expectations: The response explains that the Sui framework dependency is now resolved automatically by the CLI and should not be specified in Move.toml
The response instructs the user to remove the Sui = { git = ... } line from [dependencies]
The response explains that this change was introduced in Sui CLI v1.63+
The response shows what a correct minimal Move.toml looks like (just [package] with name and edition = '2024', empty or absent [dependencies])
The response does not suggest changing the rev field or git URL — the entire line must be removed

evals.prompt: Use this skill to set up a Sui developer environment and deploy a simple full-stack app.
evals.expected_output: A single-project workflow using MystenLabs/sui-stack-hello-world, publishing move/hello-world, then wiring the existing ui app to the new package ID.
expectations: The response uses exactly one project root cloned from https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui-stack-hello-world
The response publishes the package from sui-stack-hello-world/move/hello-world
The response updates sui-stack-hello-world/ui/src/constants.ts with the published hello-world package ID
The response runs the existing frontend from sui-stack-hello-world/ui with pnpm install and pnpm dev
The response does not create or deploy a counter package
The response does not run sui move new for the end-to-end hello-world workflow
The response does not run npm create @mysten/dapp inside the hello-world repository
The response does not install, update, or switch Move Analyzer unless the user explicitly asks for IDE or language-server setup
